At &@bout 8.30 p.m., April 25, 1938, members of 


the French Police, wnen conducting an organized search 
of pedestrians and incoming passengers on and in the 
vicinity of Roosevelt Terminal, discovered a Chinese 
male in possession of a detective's warrant card issued 
by the Dah Dao City Government to a person other than 
himself. 

This individual was immediately escorted to the 
Political Section of the French Police, where under 
interrogation he stated that his name was CHOW DIREN CHAN 
( Fa tt xz ), aged 36, a native of Paoshan (Kiangsu). 

He was further questioned by the French Police, whe 
having ascertained that this person resided with his 
family at No.3 Refugee Camp, Luzon Road, and finding 
that he had committed no offence from a& police point 

of view, decided to hand him over to the Special Branch 
for any action deemed necessary. 

He was taken over by this office at 11.30 a.m. 
April 26, 1938 and thoroughly questioned as to his recent 
movements and activities. The following is the gist of 
his statement s- | 

Some seven years ago he was employed as a shop- 

assistant at the Yee Zung ({% Dx ) Rice Hong, Rue 
Hue. When this concern closed down, he returned to 
Yanghang near Paoshan, where he secured a position 
in the Yanghang District Guild dealing with the 


FM. 2 
G. SSM-1-38 


taking and registering of census. He retained this 


post until August 1937, when with the commencement 
of Sino-Japanese hostilities, he proceeded to Shanghai 
for safety. On September 24, 1937 he, with his wife, 
son and three daughters, was admitted to the 
International Relief Committee's No.3 Refugee vamp 

( in Luzon Road. He remained in this Camp until the 
beginning of March, 1938, but his family still 
resides there. During his residence in the camp 
he did no work and rarely left the premises. On 
leaving the Camp in March he proceeded to Pootung 
where, having a little money in his possession, he 
purchased very small quantities of rice, brought it 
to the Settlement and French Concession and sold it 
to anybody he could at a meagre profit. 

He carried on in this way, ekeing out a very 
precarious livelihood, until the middle of april, 
sometimes sleeping at the home of his cousin WAUNG 
TIEN GEE (2% AY), 29 sze van ut ( 7 #0 % hi 
Tung Chong Road, Pootung, and occasionally living 
in the No.3 Camp to be with his family. Incidentally, 
it was the existence of his cousin in Pootung that 
imbued him with the desire to leave the Camp and earn 
a few dollars in the only way he knew, i.e. the 
buying and selling of rice. 

In the early part of April CHOW encountered 
one KAO FEE ee) He ) in the vicinity of Tung Chong

in the habit of calling on WAUNG TIEN GEE, who in 
those days owned a lumber yard at Tan Tse Wan 

(FE & YS) in chapei. KAO is now chief of the 

8th Corps oi the Detsctive Squad of the Dah Dao 

City Government Police Bureau. This Corps comprises 
eight members, all unarmed, and is stationed at 

Poh Jao ( d& we ), near Minghong. During the 
conversation that followed the meeting of CHOW and 
KAO, the latter suggested that the former become 

a clerk in the corps, a proposal to which VCHOW 
assented. He commenced his new duties on April 14, 
1938 at @ monthly salary of $30.00 and was despatched 
to Poh Jao, where he was accommodated in the Corps! 
office. His work consisted of recording the daily 
activities of the corps. 

In Poh Jao there is an Autonomous Commission 
in existence and a branch police bureau (about thirty 
members) of the Dah Dao City Government. <A detachment 
of some sixty Japanese soldiers is also stationed in 
this area. The corps was engaged in locating Chinese 
“pandits" and mobile units operating in the vicinity 
of Minghong and then acting as guides for the 
Japanese, whose intention it was to raid these units. 
Since CHOW assumed his post, however, nothing of any 
importance has taken place, the district being deserted,

On April 25, CHOW returned to Tung Chong Road 
with KAC in order to make certain reports to the Dah 
Dao City Government and whilst there, received 
permission from KAO to spend the night in Shanghai 
with his family at the No.3 Refugee Camp. KAO also 
gave him @ warrant card bearing the photograph and 
name of one CHU WEN CHING (4 <(_//) ) and instructed 
CHOW to take it to this person on April 26 when he 
(CHOW) returned to Minghong. CHU is a member of the 
detective squad operating at present in Poh Jao and 
it was CHOW's intention to vroceed there on the 
morning of April 26. He was, however, taken into 
custody on the same evening (April 25) when landing 
at the Roosevelt Terminal from Pootung. 

The warrant card is drawn up in four languages 
- Chinese, English, French and Japanese and photographs 
of the same, now being prepared by the French Police, 
will be submitted later. 

CHOW, himself, was not in possession of any 
means of identification, but stated that when in 
Pootung, members of his corps all wore an armiet 
indicating their rank and position. 

CHOW, having committed no chargeable offence, 
was returned to the French Police at 5 p.m., April 26, 
1938. before being handed tack to the French

pages.en:
RECOMMANDATIONS

- Il faudra se conduire correctement
  honnêtement et prudemment

- Il faudra obéir aux ordres pour ass
  urer le service sans tenir comp
  te des difficultés et dangers

- Il faudra faire des rapports avec
  conscience et exactitude

- Il ne faudra pas se corrompre, viol
  er la loi et faire injustice aux inn
  ocents.
pages.zh:
建议

- 行为须端正、诚实且谨慎

- 须服从命令以确保勤务，不顾困难与危险

- 须 conscientiously（凭良心/认真）且准确地提交报告

- 不得腐败、违法或对无辜者不公。

pages.en:
Important informations

1. When you are on duty, you must
always carry your certificate with
you and if you are asked to produ
ce same by the person or persons
concerned, you must do so

2 When on duty, you are allowed to
carry arms, but you must not draw
your weapon unless you are forced
to do so as in the following circu
mstances, viz

A When a criminal draws his wea
pon to attack you and you have
no other means of protecting
yourself

B When armed robbers offer resi
stance and try to run away and
there are no other means to arr
est them

C When mobs suddenly assemble
and trying to create a disturba
nce and you have no other me
ans to control them.
pages.zh:
重要信息

1. 执勤时，必须始终随身携带证件，如果相关人员要求出示，必须照办。

2. 执勤时允许携带武器，但除非在下列情况下被迫使用，否则不得拔枪，即：

A 当罪犯拔枪攻击你，而你别无其他自卫手段时；

B 当武装劫匪拒捕并试图逃跑，且别无其他逮捕手段时；

C 当暴徒突然聚集并试图制造骚乱，而你别无其他控制手段时。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. __________ Y
S.1, Special Branch. 8491
REPORT
Date April 27, 1938.

Subject Arrest of a Chinese found in possession of a Dah Dao
City Government Warrant Card
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford. S J

At about 8.30 p.m., April 25, 1938, members of
the French Police, when conducting an organized search
of pedestrians and incoming passengers on and in the
vicinity of Roosevelt Terminal, discovered a Chinese
male in possession of a detective's warrant card issued
by the Dah Dao City Government to a person other than
himself.

This individual was immediately escorted to the
Political Section of the French Police, where under
interrogation he stated that his name was CHOW DIEN CHAN
(周典常), aged 36, a native of Paoshan (Kiangsu).
He was further questioned by the French Police, who
having ascertained that this person resided with his
family at No.3 Refugee Camp, Luzon Road, and finding
that he had committed no offence from a police point
of view, decided to hand him over to the Special Branch
for any action deemed necessary.

He was taken over by this office at 11.30 a.m.
April 26, 1938 and thoroughly questioned as to his recent
movements and activities. The following is the gist of
his statement :-

Some seven years ago he was employed as a shop-
assistant at the Yee Zung (怡盛) Rice Hong, Rue
Hue. When this concern closed down, he returned to
Yanghang near Paoshan, where he secured a position
in the Yanghang District Guild dealing with the

（左侧批注及印章）：
D.C. G
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 27 APR 1938）

档案号 ___ Y
S.1, 特别分部。 8491
报告
日期 1938年4月27日。

主题 逮捕一名持有大道市政府侦探证的中国男子
由 D.S. Pitts 撰写 由 S J Crawford 转呈。

1938年4月25日晚8时30分左右，法国警察成员在罗斯福码头（Roosevelt Terminal）及其附近对行人和入境乘客进行有组织搜查时，发现一名中国男子持有一张由大道市政府签发给他人的侦探证。

此人随即被护送至法国警察政治科，在审讯中他声称自己名叫 CHOW DIEN CHAN（周典常），36岁，江苏宝山籍。法国警察对其进行了进一步讯问，在查明此人携家眷居住于吕宋路第3难民收容所，且从警方角度看未犯有任何罪行后，决定将其移交给特别分部，以便采取任何认为必要的行动。

本处于1938年4月26日上午11时30分接管此人，并就其近期的行踪和活动进行了彻底讯问。以下是其供词要点：

约七年前，他在霞飞路（Rue Hue）的怡盛米行担任店员。该行倒闭后，他回到宝山附近的杨行，在杨行区公会谋得一份负责

（左侧批注及印章）：
D.C. G
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别分部 1938年4月27日）

taking and registering of census. He retained this
post until August 1937, when with the commencement
of Sino-Japanese hostilities, he proceeded to Shanghai
for safety. On September 24, 1937 he, with his wife,
son and three daughters, was admitted to the
International Relief Committee's No.3 Refugee Camp
in Luzon Road. He remained in this Camp until the
beginning of March, 1938, but his family still
resides there. During his residence in the camp
he did no work and rarely left the premises. On
leaving the Camp in March he proceeded to Pootung
where, having a little money in his possession, he
purchased very small quantities of rice, brought it
to the Settlement and French Concession and sold it
to anybody he could at a meagre profit.

He carried on in this way, ekeing out a very
precarious livelihood, until the middle of April,
sometimes sleeping at the home of his cousin WAUNG
TIEN GEE (汪天奇), 29 Sze Van Li (市苑里),
Tung Chong Road, Pootung, and occasionally living
in the No.3 Camp to be with his family. Incidentally,
it was the existence of his cousin in Pootung that
imbued him with the desire to leave the Camp and earn
a few dollars in the only way he knew, i.e. the
buying and selling of rice.

In the early part of April CHOW encountered
one KAO FEE (高飛) in the vicinity of Tung Chong

户口登记工作。他一直担任此职直到1937年8月，随着中日战事爆发，他为求安全前往上海。1937年9月24日，他与妻子、儿子和三个女儿一起被接纳进入国际救济委员会位于吕宋路的第3难民收容所。他在该收容所一直住到1938年3月初，但其家人仍居住在那里。在收容所居住期间，他没有工作，也很少离开住所。3月离开收容所后，他前往浦东，利用手中仅有的一点钱购买极少量的大米，运至公共租界和法租界，以微薄的利润卖给任何能找到的买家。

他以这种方式维持着非常不稳定的生计，直到4月中旬，有时睡在浦东同宗路市苑里29号的表亲 WAUNG TIEN GEE（汪天奇）家中，偶尔也住在第3收容所以陪伴家人。顺便提一下，正是因为在浦东有这位表亲，才使他产生了离开收容所并以他所知的唯一方式——买卖大米——赚取几块钱的念头。

Road, Pootung. CHOW has known this individual for
some six years and first met him when he (KAO) was
in the habit of calling on WAUNG TIEN GEE, who in
those days owned a lumber yard at Tan Tse Wan
(潭子湾) in Chapei. KAO is now Chief of the
8th Corps of the Detective Squad of the Dah Dao
City Government Police Bureau. This Corps comprises
eight members, all unarmed, and is stationed at
Poh Jao (北桥), near Minghong. During the
conversation that followed the meeting of CHOW and
KAO, the latter suggested that the former become
a clerk in the corps, a proposal to which CHOW
assented. He commenced his new duties on April 14,
1938 at a monthly salary of $30.00 and was despatched
to Poh Jao, where he was accommodated in the Corps'
office. His work consisted of recording the daily
activities of the corps.

In Poh Jao there is an Autonomous Commission
in existence and a branch police bureau (about thirty
members) of the Dah Dao City Government. A detachment
of some sixty Japanese soldiers is also stationed in
this area. The corps was engaged in locating Chinese
"bandits" and mobile units operating in the vicinity
of Minghong and then acting as guides for the
Japanese, whose intention it was to raid these units.
Since CHOW assumed his post, however, nothing of any
importance has taken place, the district being deserted,

路浦东段附近遇到了 KAO FEE（高飛）。CHOW 认识此人已有约六年，初次见面时，KAO 习惯拜访 WAUNG TIEN GEE，后者当时在闸北潭子湾拥有一家木材行。KAO 现任大道市政府警察局侦缉队第八队队长。该队由八名成员组成，均无武装，驻扎在闵行附近的北桥。在 CHOW 和 KAO 会面后的谈话中，后者建议前者成为队里的书记员，CHOW 同意了这一提议。他于1938年4月14日开始履行新职责，月薪30.00美元，并被派往北桥，住宿在队部办公室。他的工作是记录该队的日常活动。

在北桥，存在一个自治委员会和一个大道市政府的警察分局（约三十名成员）。该地区还驻扎着一支约六十人的日军分队。该队致力于 locating（定位/搜寻）在闵行附近活动的中国“土匪”和流动部队，然后充当日军的向导，日军意图突袭这些部队。然而，自从 CHOW 上任以来，并未发生任何重要事件，该地区已荒无人烟，

practically all the villagers and country people
having left their homes following the arrival of
the Japanese.

        On April 25, CHOW returned to Tung Chong Road
with KAO in order to make certain reports to the Dah
Dao City Government and whilst there, received
permission from KAO to spend the night in Shanghai
with his family at the No.3 Refugee Camp. KAO also
gave him a warrant card bearing the photograph and
name of one CHU WEN CHING (朱文鈞) and instructed
CHOW to take it to this person on April 26 when he
(CHOW) returned to Minghong. CHU is a member of the
detective squad operating at present in Poh Jao and
it was CHOW's intention to proceed there on the
morning of April 26. He was, however, taken into
custody on the same evening (April 25) when landing
at the Roosevelt Terminal from Pootung.

        The warrant card is drawn up in four languages
- Chinese, English, French and Japanese and photographs
of the same, now being prepared by the French Police,
will be submitted later.

        CHOW, himself, was not in possession of any
means of identification, but stated that when in
Pootung, members of his corps all wore an armlet
indicating their rank and position.

        CHOW, having committed no chargeable offence,
was returned to the French Police at 5 p.m., April 26,
1938.    Before being handed back to the French

        4月25日，CHOW 与 KAO 一同返回同宗路，向大道市政府提交某些报告，在此期间，他获得 KAO 的许可，在上海吕宋路第3难民收容所的家人处过夜。KAO 还给了他一张印有 CHU WEN CHING（朱文鈞）照片和姓名的侦探证，并指示 CHOW 在4月26日返回闵行时将证件交给此人。CHU 是目前在北桥活动的侦缉队成员，CHOW 原计划于4月26日上午前往那里。然而，他在当晚（4月25日）从浦东抵达罗斯福码头时被拘留。

        该侦探证用四种语言书写——中文、英文、法文和日文，其照片副本正由法国警察制作，稍后将提交。

        CHOW 本人没有任何身份证明文件，但他称在浦东时，他所在队的成员都佩戴表明其等级和职位的臂章。
